abstract: We study unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) for multivariate time-series forecasting: a model trained on one domain must forecast well on a related domain for which no future (label) values are used during adaptation. We curated three benchmarks with distinct source and target domains: hourly weather in hilly Shimla vs plain New Delhi (Open-Meteo ERA5), daily NSE IT vs pharma stocks (Yahoo Finance) and two electricity transformers (ETTh1 vs ETTh2).

We built LiteTCN, a 0.13–0.38 M-parameter forecaster that combines reversible instance normalisation, a dilated convolutional encoder, a DLinear-style linear path and a masked-reconstruction head. We then designed CARE-DA, an adaptation objective combining source forecasting loss, multi-kernel MMD and CORAL alignment of latent features, masked reconstruction on target windows, and an L2-SP anchor to the source weights.

Across three seeds, the designed CARE-DA objective reduces target-domain MSE relative to the un-adapted model by 3.6% (climate) and 3.3% (energy), where the supervised fine-tuning oracle gains 8.5% and 3.0%; it leaves finance unchanged. Ablations and a post-hoc sensitivity study show that feature alignment is the effective component: the variant without the self-supervised term improves on all three benchmarks (−7.8%, −6.4%, −0.6%) and on energy beats the label-using oracle. The masked-reconstruction term, contrary to our hypothesis, consistently hurts. Adversarial (DANN) and CORAL-only adaptation caused negative transfer on all benchmarks. A Streamlit interface lets users upload Domain 1 or Domain 2 CSVs and inspect inputs, actual values, forecasts and metrics.
findings: **Label-free adaptation helps where the shift is real.** On climate (hilly → plain) the best label-free variants (MMD, and CARE-DA without SSL) reduce target MSE by 7.8–7.9%, close to the 8.5% of supervised fine-tuning, and the temperature RMSE drops from 1.77 °C (source-only) to 1.39 °C with MMD. On energy, CARE-DA − SSL reduces MSE by 6.4%, more than the fine-tune oracle (3.0%) and the target-only model (which is 2.6% worse than source-only), showing that the source knowledge plus alignment is worth more than the limited target labels.

**The designed CARE-DA helps, but less than its best ablation.** Full CARE-DA improves climate by 3.6% and energy by 3.3% and never causes negative transfer, but removing the masked-reconstruction term improves all three benchmarks. The post-hoc sensitivity study confirms a monotone trend: target error increases as λ_R grows from 0 to 1 on every benchmark.
**Alignment is the working core.** Removing the MMD + CORAL terms (CARE − align) turns every benchmark into negative transfer (+5.8%, +4.5%, +0.6%), even though the anchor and SSL are kept.

**Adversarial and covariance-only alignment are unstable for regression.** DANN (+5.5%, +25.7%, +2.0%) and Deep CORAL (+7.1%, +11.4%, +2.0%) are worse than doing nothing. DANN's latent discrepancy grows during training (MMD² ≈ 1.9 on climate), i.e. the min-max game does not converge with this small encoder.

**Smaller feature discrepancy does not imply better forecasts.** Full CARE-DA reaches the lowest latent MMD² on climate (0.016 vs 0.078 before adaptation) but forecasts worse than MMD-only (MMD² 0.042). Alignment must preserve forecast-relevant information, which is exactly the λ* term of the bound.
**The anchor matters when the shift is strong.** On energy, removing the anchor removes almost the whole gain (−0.1% vs −3.3%); on climate and finance its effect is small.

**Label-free adaptation does not forget Domain 1.** CARE-DA and MMD change Domain 1 test MSE by −1% to −4% (they slightly improve it), whereas supervised fine-tuning on Domain 2 increases Domain 1 error by 14% (climate) and 6% (energy).

**Finance: little to gain.** Even the oracle only improves finance by 2.4%; returns are close to unpredictable and the IT/pharma feature distributions differ mainly in level, which per-domain scaling and RevIN already remove. We report this as a genuine negative result.
sensitivity: λ_R (masked reconstruction): target MSE is lowest at λ_R = 0 on all three benchmarks and increases monotonically up to λ_R = 1 (climate 0.233 → 0.245, energy 0.160 → 0.163, finance 0.560 → 0.563). Our interpretation is that reconstructing masked input values rewards features that encode fine-grained input detail, which competes with the forecast-relevant, domain-invariant features that alignment tries to build.

λ_A (anchor): on energy the default λ_A = 0.01 gives the lowest error (0.169 without the anchor vs 0.163); on climate and finance the effect is within ±0.5%. The anchor therefore acts as a safety term against drifting, which matters most when the domain shift is large.
discussion: **Normalisation first.** Per-domain z-scoring and RevIN remove most of the level/scale (marginal) shift; for example, the 13 °C mean temperature difference between Shimla and Delhi is invisible to the encoder. The remaining shift concerns dynamics and cross-variable structure, which is what feature alignment addresses.

**Why our SSL hypothesis failed.** Test-time training works for classification when the pretext and main tasks share features. For forecasting, masked reconstruction of the look-back window is a different objective from predicting the future, and with a shared 128-d bottleneck it pulls capacity away from forecasting. A forecasting-consistent pretext, for example predicting the last part of the target window from the first part, is a better candidate.

**Model selection without labels** remains the key open problem of UDA. We used a fixed number of adaptation epochs; DANN's instability shows that an unsupervised selection criterion (e.g. reverse validation or source-risk + discrepancy) is needed before adversarial methods can be used safely.

**Limitations.** Three seeds per setting; one source/target pair per benchmark; hyper-parameters of baselines were not tuned per benchmark (same as ours); the ETT oracle gap is small (3%), which makes gap-closure ratios unstable. We therefore report relative MSE change as the main cross-benchmark metric and gap-closure computed from seed-averaged errors.

**Deployment choice.** The interface now ships CARE-DA v2 (seed 0). The original v1 checkpoint is kept as `adapted_model_v1.pt` and can be overlaid in the app. v2 was chosen after the v1 ablations showed that masked reconstruction hurts, and uses only unlabeled target inputs plus an unsupervised selection score (source-val MSE + feature MMD).
future: Verify the three datasets with the TAs; add further target domains (a coastal city, single stocks, more ETT stations) to test robustness of the conclusions.

CARE-DA v2 is now implemented (seed-0): drop masked reconstruction, add inner-horizon forecast pretext, input-view consistency, multi-scale MMD and spectral alignment, and unsupervised checkpoint selection (source-val MSE + feature MMD). Target MSE vs source-only: climate −6.2% (v1 −2.5%), energy −7.8% (v1 −3.5%), finance −1.8% (v1 +0.2%). Repeat over 3 seeds before replacing the main table.
Unsupervised hyper-parameter and checkpoint selection (reverse validation, source risk + discrepancy) so that λ can be chosen without target labels.
Few-shot extension: 1–5% labeled target windows combined with CARE-DA, and a comparison with DAF-style attention sharing.
Interface: batch upload of multiple files, per-variable metric breakdown and uncertainty bands; final stage-wise report and presentation.
